title: Symphony of Wind, Light and Life
team: Haotian Alex Xue & Yihao Ryan Chen
captions: Urban history, landscape, and community needs
Three experiential zones and the masterplan
Spatial studies and the long section
Wind Walk, Light Pavilion, and Garden Walk
intro: A post-war urban seed library and public landscape that reconnects people with nature, memory, and one another.
body: An underused urban space becomes a sensory journey through three experiences: the Wind Walk, the Light Pavilion, and the Garden Walk. Valley winds, shifting light, and Sarajevo’s tradition of home gardening inform spaces for play, rest, cultivation, and collective gathering.
body2: A living seed library invites residents to exchange, grow, and learn from local plants. Ecological renewal becomes a shared civic practice, with public space supporting everyday encounters and collective healing.

title: Re-Salting
captions: Salt experiments and a three-layer civic infrastructure
Plans and exterior perspectives
Sections, elevations, and interior atmosphere
intro: A salt shed that brings municipal infrastructure, public space, and material education into a shared urban landscape.
body: The proposal exposes the spatial and aesthetic qualities of salt: natural dunes, crystalline textures, and shifting volumes. A three-layer system preserves storage and redistribution below, introduces a public terrace in the middle, and gives the roof a silhouette informed by geological formations.
body2: Seasonal rhythms and day–night differences organize logistical flows and public activities. The industrial facility becomes a civic interface where essential operations and everyday public experience can coexist.

title: Sharing Above Park
short: A shared ground for urban living.
captions: Exploded axonometric and the layers of shared space
Residential plans and spatial studies
Elevations, sections, and collective thresholds
intro: A residential complex exploring the changing boundary between public and private life.
body: Two residential volumes are lifted above a public platform. An urban ground level, a courtyard connected to the park, and communal rooftop programs create a sequence of shared spaces between domestic life and the city.
body2: Partially shared balconies and accessible terraces encourage encounters while retaining places for individual retreat. Privacy is approached as a condition shaped through proximity and thresholds, with architecture mediating among people, nature, and urban activity.

title: A Home for Us
captions: Community programs and layered circulation
Plans and sectional relationships
Public entrance and interior perspective
intro: A youth-centered community space that connects a new rail station with places for care and everyday public life.
body: House-like volumes form a gradient of privacy. Open programs activate the ground plane, while elevated wooden volumes accommodate counseling, studios, and health services. The proposal asks how transit investment can support existing communities.
body2: Frosted glass, wood, and reflective metal articulate different thresholds. Rooftop gardens and sports terraces extend the idea of home into collective outdoor space, bringing mobility, care, and public life together.

title: Under Cantilever
short: A long life for materials and space.
team: Haotian Alex Xue & Yihao Ryan Chen
captions: Site, material lifespans, and reclamation strategy
Structural systems, testing, and assembly
Plans, circulation, and physical models
Sectional perspective and detail model
Proposed transitions: reclamation center, marketplace, and pier
intro: A building material reclamation center designed as a durable framework for changing uses and environmental conditions.
body: Prestressed and post-tensioned concrete enable a large cantilever and flexible, column-free space for receiving, sorting, and redistributing reclaimed materials. Separate circulation accommodates trucks and processing at ground level, with offices above.
body2: The design studies how a durable structure could adapt as sea levels and urban needs change. A sequence of possible futures—from reclamation center to marketplace to pier—extends reuse from individual materials to the life of an entire building.

title: Texture of the City
short: Reading the city through its traces.
captions: Exhibition, mixed-media artwork, Shikumen research, and postcards
intro: An exhibition bringing together artwork, architectural research, and observations of Shanghai’s urban texture.
body: The exhibition connects personal readings of the city with collective research on Shikumen heritage. Mixed-media work, postcards, spatial studies, and exhibition design offer different ways of looking at the city and its everyday traces.
body2: The portfolio documents individual artwork alongside group research and exhibition work developed through Issue Studio.

title: London, in Print
captions: Zines and research representations from the London semester
intro: Zine studies of the V&A Museum and Laban Dance Centre.
body: Editorial layouts, photographs, and graphic studies bring architectural observations into a compact printed format. The work explores the zine as a tool for organizing and communicating research.
body2: Produced during the Fall 2024 London study-abroad semester.

title: London Urban Studies
captions: Highgate and Wood Green studies, physical representations, and AR experiments
intro: Community research translated into modular studies, physical representations, and experiments with augmented reality.
body: Studies of Highgate and Wood Green examine the relationship between urban form and community life. A modular proposal for the old Highgate train station and a workplace palette emerge from neighborhood research.
body2: Physical studies use a wheel to represent changing housing types and social composition, and strings to represent rooftop wires. AR is explored as another way to engage with design representations.

title: Black Citizen Brigade
short: An identity for a local archive.
captions: Branding and archiving standards proposal, shown alongside exhibition identity work
intro: A branding and archiving standards proposal for a local vintage shop in Syracuse.
body: The study assembles a visual language and an approach to organizing a vintage collection. The portfolio presents the identity proposal through graphic applications and archive-related studies.
body2: Developed as a proposal in Spring 2026.

title: I over X
captions: Exhibition identity proposal, shown alongside the vintage-shop branding study
intro: A graphic identity proposal for an exhibition about self-exploration.
body: The project explores an exhibition identity through typographic marks and graphic variations. Its visual studies consider how a concise symbol can carry a theme across different applications.
body2: Developed as a proposal in Fall 2023.

intro: Historical research, cultural-access mapping, and The Gowanus Gazette.

title: Gowanus Flow
team: Haotian Alex Xue, Amara Leazer & Kaylee Ngitit
intro: A physical board game exploring infrastructure, weather, and collective responsibility.

title: Fable of Watertown
short: Cultural memory and the changing identity of water towns.
team: Haotian Alex Xue & Yihao Ryan Chen
intro: Relief painting, video projection, and sound examine tourism, cultural memory, and the transformation of Chinese water towns.
